newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury clarifies settlement on indexed notes.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury clarifies settlement on indexed notes.

text.p: The Treasury Department on Wednesday issued a calculation for the settlement amounts that investors need to pay for the 9-3/4-year inflation-indexed notes that were auctioned on Tuesday.
The $8 billion of notes are to be issued on April 15 and mature on Jan 15, 2007.
The calculation published by Treasury is based on the announced adjusted price per 100 of 98.307 and the adjusted accrued interest per thousand of 8.43846.

Thus, an investor buying a $1,000 face value note would pay the adjusted price of $983.07 plus accrued interest of $8.43846 for a total of $991.51 that must be presented at settlement on April 15 in order to receive the note.

The inflation-indexed notes auctioned on Tuesday were a reopening of the 10-year notes sold late in January. Since they carry the same Jan 15 issue date as the first issue a buyer must pay some accrued interest on the second issue.

The notes auctioned on Tuesday carry a coupon rate of 3-3/8 percent. Their principal value is adjusted daily based on changes in the Consumer Price Index in order to protect buyers against having the principal eaten away by inflation.
